problem.title: At least 149 points with no three collinear in a 75 by 75 integer grid
problem.statement: Construct 149 or 150 distinct lexicographically ordered integer points in {0,...,74}^2 with no three collinear.
problem.quantifiers: there exists a set of 149 or 150 points in the 75 by 75 grid
conventions: lexicographic ordering by x then y; every rational slope and every unordered triple is checked
completion_criteria: Supply exactly 149 or 150 distinct in-bounds lexicographically ordered integer points and pass every exact integer cross-product triple check.
sources: OP-000008 frozen card and R10-R12 snapshots dated 2026-10-26; refresh within 24 hours before launch

formal_scope: Formal OP-000008 submission: exactly 149 or 150 lexicographic points and every unordered triple; a program pass is a candidate pending scientific review.
research_scope: Research-only grid75 baseline or partial witness: 1..148 lexicographic noncollinear points; never a formal 149/150 submission or a global exclusion.

success.coordinates: JSON integers, not booleans or floats
success.triple_coverage: all unordered triples by exact integer cross product
success.150_meaning: attains the elementary upper bound and determines this instance

public_baselines.claim: 148-point public baseline; no public 149 found in directed review

one fixed-seed fixed-neighborhood exhaustive result or one row/slope-conflict lemma with complete proof text; never global nonexistence
